title: Canonical module projection mate and section comparisons
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring. Use the actual unbounded derived categories of internal $\Lambda_T$-modules and the canonical adjunction $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction], with the relative derived tensor and the specified canonical comparison $\delta_{f,M,N}:Lf^*(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)\to Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lf^*N$ [new-proetale-derived-module-pullback-monoidal]. For a scheme map $f:Z\to B$, $M\in D(B)$ and $N\in D(Z)$, define $\pi_{f,M,N}:M\otimes^{\mathbf L}Rf_*N\to Rf_*(Lf^*M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)$ as the adjoint transpose of $\delta_{f,M,Rf_*N}$ followed by $1\otimes c_{f,N}$.
For scheme maps $r:V\to X$ and $i:X\to V$ with $i\gg r=1_X$, define $l: Lr^*\mathbin{\circ}Li^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ (functor notation in order of application) by the inverse of the published pullback-composition comparison [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], transport along $i\gg r=1_X$, and the canonical identity comparison [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. Define $s:Ri_*\mathbin{\circ}Rr_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ as the adjunction conjugate of $l^{-1}$ under the composite of the specified adjunctions and the identity adjunction. Thus these are corresponding canonical composition identifications, not arbitrary isomorphisms.
